instructions: Finely chop the onion and mince the 2 garlic cloves.

Melt the 2 tbsp butter in a large pot over medium heat. Add the onion and 1/4 tsp of the salt. Cook for 10 to 12 minutes, stirring now and then, until the onion is soft and golden. Don't rush the onions. That's where the flavor starts.
Add the garlic and cook for about 1 minute, stirring, until it smells fragrant.
Meanwhile, chop 2 tbsp of the basil leaves.
Add the tomatoes with all their juice, 1 cup of the broth, the chopped basil, 1 1/2 tsp sugar, the remaining 1/4 tsp salt and the 1/4 tsp pepper. Stir and bring it to a boil over medium high heat.
Turn the heat down to low, set the lid on partway and simmer for 10 minutes, stirring once or twice.

Take the pot off the heat and blend the soup with a stick blender until it's smooth. If you're using a regular blender, fill it only halfway, hold the lid down with a towel and blend in batches, then pour it back into the pot.
Grate 3 tbsp of the parmesan. Set the pot back over medium heat and stir in the 1/4 cup cream and the grated parmesan. Bring it back to a gentle simmer, then turn off the heat.
Taste it. If it's flat, add a pinch more salt.
Ladle it into bowls and top each one with a little more grated parmesan and a few torn basil leaves. Serve with a grilled cheese sandwich or crusty bread.
method_notes: Both versions soften onion and garlic in fat, simmer canned crushed tomatoes with broth for about 10 minutes, and finish with heavy cream, fresh basil and a little sugar to round off the acid. Natasha's Kitchen cooks the onions in butter until golden, simmers the basil in the soup, blends it smooth and stirs in parmesan with the cream. Taste of Home uses green onion in olive oil, adds the basil and a splash of sherry at the end and leaves the soup unblended. This follows Natasha's Kitchen at half the batch for 4, with vegetable broth in place of chicken stock so it stays vegetarian.
